summary: Round 27 plan check, 28 Sep ~16:10Z (19:10 MSK). The 15:05-15:35Z outage was NOT a DNS outage. It was the laptop in Modern Standby on battery: lid closed 14:59:00Z, the power source switched to DC, and Windows disconnected the network in standby ('Adaptive Connected Standby', then 'Policy Setting', 'Austerity Battery Drain Budget Exceeded'). The 15:17Z round cron fell inside that standby. The laptop is still on battery now (Win32_Battery status 1 = discharging, 64% at 15:49Z). Every step tonight runs as a session-only cron or waiter on this machine: the probe 51 read (~21:30-22:15Z), the exp89l build and dummy, the 23:33Z freeze and the 00:04Z night batch. So the biggest risk to the plan is power and standby, not the models. Other findings: (2) the probe-51 read rule codes L_hi > 10.2 h as '?' with no poll-gap exception, so one more standby around 22:27Z would flip the night stack from exp89r to exp89q; (3) round 26's 'DIS 2.25 dummies run +15-20% slower' is refuted, since the extra time sits entirely in the pre-tracking stage that DIS cannot touch; (4) the same noise makes runtime rule v2 able to force a needless re-run of the exp89l dummy; (5) small gaps: no 19:30Z V_pub notify job, no 01:17Z round cron, no submit-retry rule, card v4 not stored. No E10 trigger (public notebooks max 0.953). No new disclosed knob: the only new comment on 743929 is 'this is overfitting brother. shake up is coming'. We are now rank 138 (was 134), 14th of 21 in the 0.958 block.

findings.what: Root cause of the '15:05-15:35Z DNS outage': Windows Modern Standby on battery, not the network. Kernel-Power events: 14:59:00Z enter standby (Reason: Lid); 14:59:01Z 'Power source change'; 14:59:11Z 'Connectivity state in standby: Disconnected, Reason: Adaptive Connected Standby'; 15:15:31Z a brief wake, then back into standby ('Austerity Battery Drain Budget Exceeded'; 15:15:42Z 'Disconnected, Reason: Policy Setting'); 15:39:48Z exit (Lid). The poll header 2026-09-28T15:15:31Z, with two NameResolutionErrors, is that brief wake. The 15:17Z research-round cron fell inside the standby and was lost. The machine is ON BATTERY NOW (BatteryStatus 1 = discharging, 64% at 15:49Z). Earlier idle-timeout standbys on AC (e.g. 06:49-07:31Z, 12:29-12:33Z) kept the network: the poller's 10-minute cadence stayed unbroken from 06:22Z to 12:53Z. So AC connected standby is survivable; battery or lid-closed standby cuts the network and the crons. The display-off timeout is 300 s on AC and DC, and every 'Idle Timeout' entry comes from it. Everything tonight is session-only on this laptop: the probe 51 waiter (pid 30908), the exp89l build and dummy at 51's read, the W4 FREEZE (cron 5ece5d24, 02:33 MSK) and the NIGHT BATCH (cron 2ab38c73, 03:04 MSK; 3 files, 00:05/00:06/00:46Z). Battery or lid standby at 03:04 MSK, or a flat battery, loses the 29 Sep night slots, and with them every morning decision, since the morning table keys on the night reads.

findings.what: The probe-51 read rule (R25-A1 (4); 12:16Z line) codes 'L_hi > 10.2 h' as '?' with no poll-gap exception. The PC24-08 GAP RULE (07:43Z (4)) covers only the non-CI 8.0 h case. 10.2 h after 56640366's submit (12:14:57Z) is 22:27Z, right inside the expected completion window (21:30-22:15Z, tail ~23:09Z). If the poller misses a poll again (standby, PC27-01), for example from 22:10Z to 22:40Z, a probe 51 that finished at 22:15Z gets L_hi about 10.4 h. That codes '?', and by the 12:25Z night rule exp89q replaces exp89r even if 51 displays 0.959. The '?' code is there to catch skipped insertion. Insertion is fail-soft and only lowers the score, so a display that clears REF is valid evidence whatever the insertion state.

findings.what: REFUTED: round 26 new fact 6 / WATCHLIST I306 ('the DIS 2.25 dummies ran +15-20% vs their siblings'). The whole difference sits in the silent pre-tracking stage, between the ~46 s dependency/config lines and the 'V1284 head patched ... mode = candidate' line. DIS is an ILP weight and cannot act there. Time from 'mode = candidate' to the end: exp89p 1,060 s vs exp89q 1,057 s; exp85a 1,126 s vs exp89s 1,130 s; exp88b 1,153 s vs exp88a 1,106 s. ILP on 6bba_05db0fb1: 76.8 s (89p) vs 76.7 s (89q); 76.1 s (85a) vs 79.6 s (89s). Pre-stage end: exp89p 253 s vs exp89q 519 s; exp85a 262 s vs exp89s 436 s; exp88a 788 s. That is machine or I/O noise of up to ~535 s between siblings. Consequence: the hidden latency of exp89q/exp89s equals the K2 safetail band (6.87-7.81 h), and exp89r's equals the CI band. There is no extra risk from the DIVINS 8 h or CI 10.5 h deadline. The morning timing (exp89s by 11:30Z reads by ~19:18Z) is unchanged.

findings.what: The night checklist (R26-A4 (c)) has no rule for a submit command that fails or times out. That is likely after today's network drops. 'kaggle competitions submit' can fail on the client after Kaggle has already accepted the file. A blind retry then spends a second 29 Sep slot on the same file (5/day; the night uses 3) and co-completes two identical refs, which masks the UP test. The pre-submit checks cover duplicates only before the first attempt.

EXP75 PARTNER RULE v2 already puts pair A {V_pub, #37} first in that case. The morning table's only non-CI candidate that could become V_pub in branch B, exp89s (K + DIS 2.25, dummy PASS 14:40Z), would then be sent only after exp89q and exp89p read (decision by 10:30Z, read ~18:00-18:20Z, after the 18:37Z proposal draft). Sending exp89s at night instead (01:26Z, >= 40 min after exp89p) gives a direct K+DIS read by ~09:15Z, well before the finals, and frees the morning slot. This changes a user-confirmed night slot, so it needs the user's yes. The default is to keep exp75.
